AWARD/JUDGMENT FACTUAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 1.
This DAR was filed on 14/11/2022 by the Investigating Officer in the presence of the parties.
The DAR is related to a motor vehicular accident dated 19/05/2022 in which one Sh. Ghanshyam S/o Sh. Vishwanath (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained grievous injuries.

As per petitioner, on 19/05/2022 at about 07.30 AM, he was going to Azadpur Mandi from Jharoda loading spinach (palak) on his Thela-Rickshaw which was pulling by him at a normal speed and on correct side of the road and when he reached at R.C.C. Road infront of Gate, Hardev Nagar,
Nirankari Ground, Jharoda, Delhi falling within the jurisdiction of PS Wazirabad in the meanwhile a RTV Bus bearing registration number DL-1VC-3354 (hereinafter referred to as "offending vehicle")
which was being driven by its driver/ R-1 at a very high speed, rashly, negligently, without taking necessary precautions, without proper lookout, violating the traffic rules without blowing any horn came and hit on him at a great force on back side.

It is further stated that as a result of this he fell down on PANKAJ by PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.10.03 11:08:05 +0530 the road due to which he sustained grievous injuries and other multiple injuries all over his body.

It is further stated that thereafter he was taken to Aakar Multispeciality Hospital, near Primary School, Mandoli,
Delhi-110093 where he was medically examined by the doctor and vide MLC was prepared by the doctors.

It is further stated that he has incurred Rs.5,703/- on his medical treatment, Rs.50,000/-
on special diet and Rs.50,000/- on conveyance and Rs.60,000/- for attendant charges.
It is further stated that at the time of accident the petitioner was 45 years old and was working as Rickshaw Puller in Delhi and he was earning Rs.20,000/- to Rs.25,000/- per month approx.

An FIR no.
576/22 U/s 279/338 IPC PS Wazirabad was registered by the police with respect to above accident.
R-1 is stated to be the driver of the offending vehicle.
R-2 is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
DAR was treated as a claim petition.
R-1 and R-2 were also directed to file their Written Statements.

2. No written statement was filed by R-1 and accordingly right to file written statement on behalf of R-1 was closed vide order dated 26/03/2024 passed by this Tribunal.
3. A written statement was filed by R-2 wherein it is stated that the offending vehicle has been falsely implicated by the police as no accident, as alleged in the petition, ever took place.

On merits,
the contents of petition have been denied in toto.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.10.03 11:08:26 +0530 Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed while the petitioner was going on motorcycle and hit his motorcycle at the relevant time.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
13. In view of the medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

"Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

15. As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The PANKAJ PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date: 2024.10.03 11:08:42 +0530 pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just'
compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs.
Pest Control
( India) Pvt. Ltd.,

(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.

The petitioner has placed on judicial file his medical papers and medical bills, which are Ex.
PW1/2 (Colly) and Ex. PW1/3(Colly).

As per the medical bills Ex.PW1/4 (Colly), the petitioner has Ghanshyam(I)(Fir ... vs Manoj Shukla on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58963308/

In the absence of any contest to the said documents (placed on record by the petitioner), the petitioner is held entitled to an amount of Rs.5,703/- under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 19.
As per medical documents, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and PANKAJ

Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs. 50,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of actual earnings 20.
In his affidavit Ex. PW1/A, the petitioner claims that he was a rickshaw puller and was earning Rs. 22,000/- to Rs.25,000/-- per month approx from that vocation.
The medical documents reflect that the petitioner sustained a grievous injuries.
The above documents are sufficient to uphold the claim of the petitioner to the effect that he was unable to resume his work for about 03 months due to the injuries.

In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the Minimum Wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi ( petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi) as on the date of accident.
As per relevant notification, the minimum wages admissible to an Unskilled person as he was and as on 01/04/2022 in Delhi were Rs.16,506-.
As such, the petitioner is held entitled to a sum of Rs.49,518/- (Rs.16,506/- X 3).
The said sum is awarded to the petitioner under this head.
(iv) Conveyance, Attendant Charges and Special Diet & Amenities of life 21.
In view of the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and the extended period of medical treatment, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs. 35,000/- each under these heads.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
The petitioner claims compensation on account of special pecuniary damage relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicine, transportation, diet, loss of earning during the period, he was injured, loss of earning during the period of treatment, loss of future earning on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, non-pecuniary damages, damages for pain suffering and trauma, loss of amenities and loss of expectation of life.
There is nothing on record which betrays any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PW-1.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW- 1 is reliable and trustworthy.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant time, R-1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed while the petitioner was going on motorcycle and hit his motorcycle at the relevant time.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
16. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non- pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just'
compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Further, in case of permanent disability, the assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future earning, would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on his earning capacity.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and PANKAJ
In the absence of any material as to the monthly earnings of the petitioner, it would be appropriate to assume the monthly earnings of the petitioner as per the Minimum Wages payable to an unskilled person in Delhi ( petitioner being an ordinary resident of Delhi) as on the date of accident.
